context.buying_mechanics: Out-of-home advertising is purchased through several mechanisms depending on format: (1) Traditional OOH (static billboards, posters, transit shelters) is bought direct from operators (Lamar, Clear Channel, JCDecaux, Outfront) via insertion order for specific faces and flight periods—typically 4-week cycles; (2) Digital OOH (DOOH) is bought direct from operators or programmatically via DSPs like The Trade Desk, Hivestack, Vistar Media, and Place Exchange, which aggregate digital screens across networks; (3) Programmatic DOOH (pDOOH) enables real-time, audience-triggered buying—ads play on screens when target audience members are geographically proximate, based on mobile device location data. OOH is measured by gross impressions (traffic counts × display frequency) using the Geopath audience measurement system in the US.
context.measurement_approaches: Traditional OOH measurement relies on Geopath mobility data (mobile GPS and traffic counts) to estimate audience impressions by demographic and DMA. CPM-equivalent metrics are standard for planning purposes. DOOH adds digital-native metrics: play count (verified ad displays), share of voice in digital pods (percentage of total loop time owned), and viewability estimation via camera-based attention data (VIOOH, Alfi) on select screens. Campaign attribution has improved significantly: mobile device ID tracking enables conversion lift measurement by comparing in-store visits, website visits, or app downloads from devices exposed to OOH locations vs. unexposed control groups. Brand lift studies via survey methodology are also standard for larger campaigns.
context.typical_cpms: National large-format billboard (static): $3–$10 CPM; urban transit shelters and bus wraps: $5–$15 CPM; digital billboard (DOOH) at high-traffic intersections: $10–$25 CPM; programmatic DOOH (pDOOH): $8–$20 CPM depending on audience targeting precision; airport advertising: $15–$40 CPM; Times Square / iconic urban placements: $40–$100+ CPM; venue-based OOH (gyms, airports, stadiums, bars, restaurants): $10–$35 CPM; street furniture (bus shelters, kiosks): $8–$18 CPM. CPMs vary dramatically by location, market, and traffic density.
targeting_capabilities: Geographic targeting by DMA, metro, city, neighborhood, zip code, or specific address radii
Contextual/venue targeting (airports, gyms, convenience stores, bars, transit stations, retail corridors)
Audience targeting via programmatic DOOH using mobile device location data (behavioral segments in proximity to screens)
Time-of-day and daypart targeting (morning commute, lunch, evening rush, weekend) for DOOH
Weather-triggered dynamic creative (ad content adapts to temperature, precipitation, or weather conditions)
Competitive conquesting (buying screens near competitor locations)
common_pitfalls: Designing creative with too much text or detail—the 3-second rule applies to OOH; complex messaging is impossible to process at 65mph
Buying static OOH without considering dwell time of the medium—billboards on 65mph highways have 3-second average views; airport/transit provides 10+ seconds
Failing to coordinate OOH with digital retargeting—exposed mobile devices near OOH screens can be captured for follow-up digital advertising, dramatically improving attribution
Over-concentrating spend in one large format instead of distributing across a market for cumulative frequency
Ignoring production costs and lead times for static OOH—vinyl installation, printing, and permitting can add 3–4 weeks of lead time
Not measuring OOH's contribution to lift—attribution is now possible via mobile device matching and store visit measurement, but many brands skip this step
formats: Bulletins / large-format billboards (14x48 ft, highest-visibility highway placements)
Digital billboards / large DOOH (rotating 6–8 second ad slots, dynamic creative capable)
Street furniture (bus shelters, newsstands, transit kiosks—pedestrian-level, high dwell time)
Transit advertising (bus wraps, subway/rail station dominations, airport displays)
Place-based DOOH (gyms, bars, restaurants, convenience stores, office elevators—venue-specific audiences)
Spectacular / wallscapes (building wraps, 3D anamorphic installations for major brand moments)
key_platforms: Lamar Advertising (largest US OOH operator, 165,000+ displays)
Clear Channel Outdoor (global OOH operator, Smart Audience targeting platform)
Outfront Media (US OOH operator, strong transit position)
JCDecaux (global, strong in transit and urban street furniture)
Hivestack (programmatic DOOH SSP and DSP, global scale)
Place Exchange (programmatic OOH exchange, The Trade Desk integration)
Geopath (US audience measurement body for OOH)
context.planning_considerations: OOH's defining characteristics are its inability to be skipped, blocked, or fast-forwarded, and its physical presence in the real world. It is one of the few channels that cannot be ad-blocked. Planning considerations: (1) OOH is fundamentally a reach channel—it builds brand awareness through repeated geographic impressions; (2) creative must communicate in 3–5 seconds for highway/transit placements; longer dwell contexts (airports, elevators) allow more complex messaging; (3) programmatic DOOH allows dynamic creative delivery (weather triggers, live sports scores, countdown timers) that static cannot; (4) local market activation (DMAs, cities) is OOH's greatest strength—brands can dominate a specific geography efficiently; (5) OOH pairs well with digital retargeting of exposed device IDs.
context.trend_2026: DOOH now represents approximately 67% of total OOH spend in major markets, surpassing static as the dominant format. Global OOH spend is on track to reach $49.8B in 2025. Programmatic DOOH spending is projected to reach $1.22B in the US in 2026, growing 22.6% YoY. Measurement innovation—particularly mobile device location matching for attribution and store visit lift—is making OOH more defensible in data-driven media plans. Retail media is integrating with OOH as retailers install DOOH screens within stores (in-store retail media screens). AI-powered creative optimization for DOOH (dynamic content personalization by audience, time, and context) is moving from experimental to standard. OOH operators are investing in first-party audience data strategies to compete with digital platforms.
context.integration_with_other_channels: OOH is most powerful when integrated with digital channels to create a closed-loop ecosystem. Key integrations: (1) OOH + mobile retargeting—devices exposed to OOH placements are served follow-up mobile ads within hours; (2) OOH + paid search—OOH brand building drives branded search queries; QR codes on OOH bridge the physical-digital gap; (3) OOH + social—OOH activations (spectaculars, 3D installs) generate social sharing and earned media, amplifying paid reach; (4) OOH + audio—commuters see billboards while listening to podcasts/radio, creating multi-sense impression.
context.budget_allocation_guidance: OOH typically represents 5–15% of media budgets for local/regional advertisers and 5–10% for national advertisers. Most effective for campaigns requiring geographic dominance, location-specific targeting (near retail, competitor locations, or events), or cultural moment activations where physical presence matters. Minimum viable OOH investment for a single DMA campaign: $15,000–$30,000/month for meaningful coverage. Increase OOH allocation for local market launches, retail-driven campaigns, or campaigns targeting consumers in specific physical contexts (gym, transit, airport). Reduce when the campaign is purely direct-response digital with no need for geographic presence or ambient brand building.
